y1: Jesus leaves Galilee and goes to Judea across the Jordan. The final journey toward the cross begins. The Pharisees tested Him with the issue of divorce, but Jesus goes back to the beginning of creation and speaks of the sanctity of marriage.
y2: Then comes the scene with the children. The disciples hindered them, but Jesus says, 'The kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.' The children have nothing to show off, so they are able to receive. This connects with 18:3.
y3: In 19:3–12, based on Genesis 1–2, Jesus says that marriage is something God has joined together, while also stating that singleness for the kingdom of God is valuable. Both paths are lives dedicated to God.
y5: The young man asked, 'What good thing must I do to get eternal life?' He thought of eternal life as an 'achievement to be done.' Jesus quotes the commandments regarding neighbors from the Ten Commandments and adds the command to 'love your neighbor as yourself.'
y6: 'I have kept all these, what do I still lack?' Jesus says, 'If you want to be perfect, go, sell your possessions, give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me.' Because the young man had great wealth, he went away sad.
y7: Jesus only mentioned the commandments related to neighbors. Then, with the words 'sell your possessions,' He tested the first commandment ('You shall have no other gods before me'). The young man's true god was his wealth. The words in 6:24, 'You cannot serve both God and wealth,' became a reality.
y9: 'It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.' The camel was the largest animal in Palestine, and the eye of a needle was the smallest hole. It is an intentional impossibility.
y10: At that time, wealth was considered proof of God's blessing. Therefore, the disciples were amazed and asked, 'Who then can be saved?' Jesus' answer: 'With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.' Salvation is not an achievement, but God's work.
y11: There is an explanation that there was a small gate in Jerusalem called the 'eye of a needle,' and a camel had to unload its burden and kneel to pass through it, but there is no historical basis for this. Jesus said 'impossible,' not 'difficult,' meaning that only God can do it.
y13: Peter said, 'See, we have left everything and followed You. What then will we have?' They were people who made the opposite choice of the young man.
y14: Jesus promises that in the new world they will sit on twelve thrones, and will receive a hundredfold of what they left behind, and eternal life. But at the end, He gives a warning: 'Many who are first will be last, and many who are last will be first.' This leads into the parable of the vineyard in the next chapter.
y15: Jesus does not scold Peter for his question, but answers with a promise. God is not one who gives nothing in return. But He shows in the next chapter that the reward is 'grace,' not a 'calculation.'
verse: “Looking at them, Jesus said, ‘With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.’”
prayer: Jesus, thank You for hugging and blessing the children who had nothing to show off. Show me the 'wealth' that holds me back, and instead of going away sad, help me to joyfully let it go and follow You. I believe that what is impossible for man is possible for God. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: good. Jesus says, 'There is only One who is good' (19:17). The measure of goodness is not my actions, but God. The young man asked about a 'good thing,' but Jesus pointed to the 'Good One.'
d1: wealth. Mainly refers to land and property. The young man was sad because of his 'great wealth.' 'For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also' (6:21).
d2: camel. There is a similar expression in Jewish writings like 'an elephant going through the eye of a needle.' It is a word that vividly shows impossibility. 'Straining out a gnat and swallowing a camel' in 23:24 is in the same style.
d3: hundredfold. Mark adds that they will receive it 'with persecutions' (Mark 10:30). It means gaining a new family and home called the church. It is also connected to the 'hundredfold crop' in 13:8.
